title: Exceptional unidirectional radiation modes
byline: An; Shuowei; Liu; Tuo; Zhu; Jie; Cheng
html:
Abstract:Singularities such as exceptional points (EPs) and bound states in the continuum (BICs) fundamentally reshape the spectral response of non-Hermitian open systems, unlocking exotic physical phenomena and unprecedented ways of wave manipulation. Nevertheless, the radiation behaviors of modes evolving around these singularities lack a unified picture. Here we show that a mode originating from a BIC can radiate unidirectionally, exhibiting a quality factor that continuously varies in parameter space from a near-infinite value (near the BIC) to a finite lower bound as it coalesces with the other (leaky) mode at an EP. The crossing of the unidirectional radiation mode and the EP in parameter space results in not only merged poles (resonant EP) but also merged zeros (absorbing EP) of the scattering matrix, along with a counterintuitive reversal of radiation direction decoupled from the coalesced eigenmodes under near-field excitation. These phenomena are experimentally observed in an acoustic waveguide system featuring two side-branch resonant cavities with deliberate frequency detuning and asymmetric dissipation. Our findings reveal the intrinsic connection between eigenmode topology and radiation behavior in open systems, offering a viable route for tailoring scattering and radiation responses via non-Hermitian modulations.
